name: argument-parser-negative-test-706c373f17/invalid-byte-p.bal
spec_references: Module-level declarations: "Supports required-params, defaultable-params, included-record-param and rest-param in the signature"
reason: The source declares an empty public main function with one required byte parameter. Its expected failure comes from supplying the command-line string 256 through the @args directive, rather than from an invalid source expression or assignment. Function definitions and required parameters are covered, but subset10 does not describe command-line entry-point invocation, conversion of argument strings to byte values, or the failure behavior for an out-of-range argument. Consequently the whole case exercises a not-covered runtime argument-parsing feature. The byte parameter's ordinary type checking alone cannot establish support for this externally supplied argument conversion and its expected panic.
unsupported_constructs: Command-line argument conversion and rejection for a byte-typed main parameter
test_design_notes: The @args and @panic comments are harness markers, not Ballerina syntax.
No panic statement occurs in the empty function body; the expected failure must occur during argument handling.
No mixed unsupported source constructs or obvious migration errors are visible.
